newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurds begin second round of peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurds begin second round of peace talks.

text.p: Rival Kurdish factions on Friday affirmed their desire to consolidate a three-week-old ceasefire in northern Iraq as their second round of U.S.-brokered talks began in Ankara.

"We will do our best to cooperate in taking the necessary measures to make sure the ceasefire holds," the head of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) delegation Mohamed Salih Cuma said before the discussions.
A delegate from the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan said his faction remained committed to a statement agreed at a first round of talks in October to reconcile the feuding groups.
U.S. diplomat Robert Pelletreau, who was mediating along with British and Turkish officials, said the session was aimed at consolidating the ceasefire and building confidence between the parties.

Pelletreau negotiated the initial ceasefire between Massoud Barzani's KDP and Jalal Talabani's PUK after nearly two months of fighting that gave President Saddam Hussein a foothold in northern Iraq after a five-year break.

The two factions began fighting after Iraqi armoured divisions backed Barzani's KDP in late August to capture the regional capital Arbil from the PUK, prompting U.S missile strikes against targets in southern Iraq.

The status of Arbil and the sharing of KDP oil trade revenues on the Turkish border are key issues that must be resolved in the longer term, mediators said. Those issues undermined a Kurdish attempt at parliamentary self-rule in northern Iraq after Western-sponsored elections in 1992.
Pelletreau said the talks would deal with humanitarian aid for northern Iraq, stressing the importance as the harsh winter approached.

He also referred to "bringing terrorism under control" but did not elaborate. Turkish officials say the power vacuum in northern Iraq enables Kurdish rebels seeking self-rule in Turkey to launch cross-border attacks.
Iraqi Kurds broke from Baghdad with encouragement from the West after Iraq's defeat in the 1991 Gulf War.
